title: Jev HTTP errors can echo the API key and drop the account error message
rawReport:
## Summary
`fetchPost` in structure-sweep's Jev client returns the raw response body on an error status. If the upstream error body echoes request material, the API key can end up in a thrown `JevAskError` message and in logs. And a terminal account error (402, credit limit) is reported only as a JSON-encoded reason, without the provider's message or code.

## What I was doing
Salvaging changes an agent had left uncommitted in the main checkout before cleaning it. This part was an independent fix worth keeping.

## What I observed
- `packages/structure-sweep/src/jev.ts` `fetchPost` passes `await response.json()` through unchanged for every status.
- `JevAskError` carries only `reason`, so a 402 with `{ error: { message: "Credit limit reached", code: "payment_required" } }` surfaces as `jev: {...}` with no readable detail.
- The salvaged fix: redact the API key from error bodies (status ≥ 400) before they leave `fetchPost`, add an optional `detail` to `JevAskError` built from `error.message` / `error.code` (bounded), and a test that a 402 surfaces "Credit limit reached; payment_required" without retrying.

## Why it matters
A secret in an exception message ends up in CI logs and bug reports. Account errors without a message make "why did the sweep stop" slow to diagnose.

## Pointers
- `packages/structure-sweep/src/jev.ts` (`fetchPost`, `JevAskError`, `httpJevClient`)
- `packages/structure-sweep/test/jev.test.ts`
- backlog-sweep may carry its own copy of the Jev client; check it too

## Suggested next step (non-binding)
Apply the salvaged patch, add a test that asserts the key never appears in a thrown message, and do the same in backlog-sweep if it has its own client.

---

enriched:
## Summary

Both Jev HTTP clients in this repo pass an error response body through unchanged, so an upstream body that echoes request material can carry the `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` into a thrown `JevAskError` message (and from there into CI logs and bug reports). The same clients also drop the provider's own account-error text: a terminal 402 surfaces only as `jev: {...}` JSON with no readable message or code.

One small PR fixes both clients.

## Where it lives (read at `origin/main`)

- `packages/structure-sweep/src/jev.ts` — `fetchPost(apiKey)` returns `{ status: response.status, body: await response.json().catch(() => ({})) }` for every status; `JevAskError` carries only `reason` and builds its message as `` `jev: ${JSON.stringify(reason)}` ``; `httpJevClient` throws it once a failure is terminal or the retry budget is spent.
- `packages/backlog-sweep/src/jev.ts` — its own copy of the same client: its own `fetchPost` and its own `JevAskError`, identical shape at the same lines. It has **no** Jev test today; `packages/backlog-sweep/test/` holds only `repo.test.ts` and `verdict.test.ts`, so its test is a new `packages/backlog-sweep/test/jev.test.ts`.
- Existing structure-sweep test: `packages/structure-sweep/test/jev.test.ts`.

## Fix shape

- In `fetchPost`, for `status >= 400`, redact every occurrence of the API key from the parsed body before it is returned (the key must never leave `fetchPost` inside an error body).
- Give `JevAskError` an optional `detail` built from the provider's `error.message` / `error.code`, bounded in length, and fold it into the error message so a 402 reads e.g. `Credit limit reached; payment_required`.
- Apply the same change to both clients. The backlog-sweep half stays confined to its Jev client file and its test.

Triage note: the salvaged patch for the structure-sweep half exists and is a reasonable starting point; it was written against an older base, so re-apply against current `main` rather than assuming it applies cleanly. Hoisting the two clients into one shared module is out of scope here.

Triage note: searched the board for an owner of the Jev client / error-redaction surface (dedup on "Jev API key redaction error body" and "jev client fetchPost JevAskError") — no open issue or epic owns it, so this stands alone.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In `packages/structure-sweep/src/jev.ts`, `fetchPost` redacts the API key from Jev HTTP error bodies (status >= 400) before they leave `fetchPost`.
- [ ] structure-sweep's `JevAskError` carries an optional bounded `detail` built from the provider's `error.message` / `error.code`.
- [ ] A structure-sweep test: a 402 with `{ error: { message: "Credit limit reached", code: "payment_required" } }` surfaces "Credit limit reached; payment_required" and is not retried.
- [ ] A new structure-sweep test asserts the API key never appears in any thrown error message, including when the error body echoes the key.
- [ ] `packages/backlog-sweep/src/jev.ts` gets the same redaction in its own `fetchPost` and the same bounded `detail` on its own `JevAskError`, with both tests above added in a new `packages/backlog-sweep/test/jev.test.ts`; the backlog-sweep change is confined to that Jev client file and its test.
- [ ] A patch changeset for each touched package: `@demlik/structure-sweep` and `@demlik/backlog-sweep`.
